extension.name: mcp-transport-negotiation
extension.what: connectToServer (memoized) builds one of seven MCP transports from ScopedMcpServerConfig: SSEClientTransport for 'sse' with an auth-provider eventSourceInit and 'sse-ide' without auth, WebSocketTransport over the Bun global WebSocket or a Node ws client for 'ws' and 'ws-ide', StreamableHTTPClientTransport for 'http' with step-up-auth detection wrapping a per-request fresh timeout, StdioClientTransport for stdio configs, and SdkControlClientTransport for in-process SDK servers (src/services/mcp/client.ts:566-762). 'sdk' explicitly throws because SDK servers are handled in print.ts, and stdio stderr is piped and capped at 64MB so server output cannot flood the UI (client.ts:193-200, 363). No feature or GrowthBook gate sits on this path.
invariants: Authorization headers are redacted before any debug log
stdio env is subprocessEnv() merged over the server's own env
an unsupported server shape throws rather than silently no-oping
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed for an unknown transport type (throws 'Unsupported MCP server transport'); fail-soft per server elsewhere, so one failed server does not stop the others

extension.name: mcp-connection-lifecycle-and-recovery
extension.what: Connections are memoized by a JSON-stringified config cache key; the SDK client's onclose handler deletes all four caches (tools, resources, commands and connectToServer) so the next operation reconnects, and an onerror wrapper counts terminal connection errors and force-closes the transport after 3, rejecting pending promises that would otherwise hang because the SSE transport never calls onclose after exhausting reconnects (src/services/mcp/client.ts:452-486, 1188-1239). useManageMCPConnections adds the UI-side policy: 5 attempts with exponential backoff from 1s to 30s, a per-server circuit breaker opening after 3 failed full cycles and suppressing automatic reconnect for 5 minutes, and manual reconnect/toggle exposed via the MCPConnectionManager context (src/services/mcp/useManageMCPConnections.ts:51-60, 148-161, 332-358). Local servers connect in batches of 3 and remote servers in batches of 20 through a slot-releasing batched runner (useManageMCPConnections.ts:795-798).
invariants: a closed connection must clear every fetch cache or stale tools are served
the circuit breaker resets on any successful connect, automatic or manual
a manual toggle persists through setMcpServerEnabled to project config
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft: repeated failures degrade to a disabled or failed server and an open circuit breaker, never a crash or a blocked agent loop

extension.name: mcp-oauth-and-xaa-auth
extension.what: Remote MCP servers authenticate through a full OAuth 2.1 flow: RFC 9728 and RFC 8414 metadata discovery, a random loopback redirect port (39152-49151 on Windows because 49152-65535 is reserved), PKCE, and token persistence into the OS secure-storage slot keyed by the server key (src/services/mcp/auth.ts:61-114; src/services/mcp/oauthPort.ts:9-13). Refresh is serialised by a cross-process lock with 5 retries and a re-read of the keychain after acquisition so a second process's refresh is reused, and invalid_grant re-checks storage for a fresh token before failing (auth.ts:2144-2178, 2302-2318). XAA (Cross-App Access, SEP-990) is a distinct path gated hard on CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_XAA with no silent fallback to the consent flow (src/services/mcp/xaaIdpLogin.ts:32-34; auth.ts:879-883).
invariants: XAA is the only path when oauth.xaa is set, and the consent flow is never used as a fallback
sensitive OAuth params (state, nonce, code, code_verifier, code_challenge) are redacted from logs
a refresh lock that cannot be acquired proceeds without the lock rather than deadlocking
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed for XAA config (throws 'XAA is not enabled' or 'no IdP connection configured'); fail-soft for background refresh, which returns undefined and falls through to the needs-auth path

extension.name: mcp-config-resolution-and-policy
extension.what: MCP server definitions are collected per scope: enterprise (exclusive — if an enterprise MCP config exists, all other sources are ignored), user, project (.mcp.json walked from the filesystem root down to cwd so nearer files win) and local, plus plugin-provided servers merged from loadAllPluginsCacheOnly (src/services/mcp/config.ts:972-1015, 812-859). Enterprise allow/deny policy is enforced at collection time with denylist precedence, name/command/URL matching, wildcard URL globs, empty-allowlist-blocks-all semantics and allowManagedMcpServersOnly restricting the allowlist to policySettings (config.ts:287-357, 1354-1358). Environment variables are expanded as ${VAR} and ${VAR:-default} and a headersHelper subprocess supplies dynamic auth headers (src/services/mcp/envExpansion.ts:16-32; src/services/mcp/headersHelper.ts:41-72). A related side mechanism, the official MCP registry lookup, is INERT because prefetchOfficialMcpUrls() is a bare return (src/services/mcp/officialRegistry.ts:33-45).
invariants: enterprise MCP config is exclusive when present
the denylist always beats the allowlist, and an empty allowlist denies everything
headersHelper is refused before workspace trust for project and local scoped servers
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed by default: a missing variable is left literal and reported, the denylist wins, and an untrusted headersHelper returns null so the connection proceeds unauthenticated rather than executing code

extension.name: mcp-instructions-and-tool-identity
extension.what: MCP tools get a canonical mcp__<normalized-server>__<normalized-tool> identity produced by normalizeNameForMCP, so permission rules can target the prefixed name and cannot be spoofed by an MCP tool reusing a builtin name (src/services/mcp/normalization.ts:10-12; src/services/mcp/mcpStringUtils.ts:39-67). Server InitializeResult instructions and tool descriptions are truncated to 2048 characters before reaching the model (src/services/mcp/client.ts:964-970). Announcing newly connected servers' instructions via persisted mcp_instructions_delta attachments is gated by isMcpInstructionsDeltaEnabled(), which is false in this build, so the pre-gate uncached system-prompt-section path is what actually runs (src/utils/mcpInstructionsDelta.ts:37-70; src/constants/prompts.ts:431).
invariants: permission checks use the fully-qualified mcp__server__tool name, never the display name
instructions and descriptions are capped at 2048 chars with a truncation marker
the delta scan diffs on server name because instructions are immutable per connection
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft: over-long text is truncated, malformed names are normalised, and a server with unparseable names still connects

extension.name: mcp-result-transformation-and-spill
extension.what: MCP tool results are normalised into model-consumable content: transformMCPResult and processMCPResult split string, content-array and structuredContent results, synthesise a JSON schema description via inferCompactSchema, compress oversized images and enforce a token cap (src/utils/mcpValidation.ts:14-78). The cap resolves as the MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS env var, then a GrowthBook value, then a hardcoded default; because GrowthBook is a stub the middle tier never applies (mcpValidation.ts:26-47; src/services/mcp/client.ts:2436-2454). When a result exceeds the cap the full payload is written to the tool-results directory and the model receives a path plus mandatory-read instructions instead of the data (src/utils/mcpOutputStorage.ts:16-59).
invariants: result size is estimated before sending, with images counted at 1600 tokens each
over-cap output is persisted to disk, never silently dropped
structured content carries its inferred schema so the model can interpret it
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft: on write failure the caller still gets a truncated or annotated result and an error is logged

extension.name: mcp-elicitation-bridge
extension.what: MCP servers can request user input mid-tool-call: registerElicitationHandler installs an ElicitRequestSchema handler that first runs Elicitation hooks — a hook response short-circuits the UI entirely — and otherwise queues an ElicitationRequestEvent into app state for the form or URL flow, with URL requests tracked by elicitationId so an ElicitationCompleteNotification can resolve them (src/services/mcp/elicitationHandler.ts:68-120). A separate retry wrapper catches McpError code -32042 (UrlElicitationRequired), drives the URL elicitation and re-invokes the tool (src/services/mcp/client.ts:2642-2684).
invariants: hooks are consulted before any user-visible prompt
URL elicitations are limited to 3 retries before the original error propagates
elicitation request params are validated (mode 'url', string url) before use
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft: an aborted signal resolves the elicitation as {action:'cancel'}, and a client created without elicitation capability is tolerated by a try/catch around setRequestHandler

extension.name: lsp-server-lifecycle
extension.what: LSP servers are supplied ONLY by plugins — getAllLspServers calls loadAllPluginsCacheOnly then getPluginLspServers per plugin, merging with later-plugin-wins — never by user or project settings (src/services/lsp/config.ts:11, 27-49). A module-scope singleton manager validates each config (command plus non-empty extensionToLanguage required), builds an extension-to-server map, and starts servers lazily on the first file operation via ensureServerStarted, answering workspace/configuration requests with nulls so servers such as TypeScript proceed (src/services/lsp/LSPServerManager.ts:88-236). initializeLspServerManager is a no-op under --bare, and reinitializeLspServerManager tears down and rebuilds after a plugin refresh (src/services/lsp/manager.ts:100-150, 226-253).
invariants: LSP config is plugin-only
a server that fails to initialise is skipped without failing the whole manager
getLspServerManager returns undefined after a failed init so callers cannot use a broken instance
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft: per-server try/catch with logging, and LSPTool.isEnabled() is false while no server is healthy

extension.name: lsp-passive-diagnostics
extension.what: Each LSP server instance gets a textDocument/publishDiagnostics notification handler that validates params, converts them to Claude's DiagnosticFile shape and registers them as a pending diagnostic for async attachment delivery, the same pattern AsyncHookRegistry uses (src/services/lsp/LSPDiagnosticRegistry.ts:42-46, 136-183). Delivery deduplicates within a batch and across turns using content-keyed sets held in a 500-entry LRU, then volume-limits to 10 diagnostics per file and 30 total, and tracks consecutive per-server failures (LSPDiagnosticRegistry.ts:229-282; src/services/lsp/passiveFeedback.ts:125-220). Registration is per-server and its failures are counted rather than thrown.
invariants: diagnostics are only marked delivered AFTER successful dedup, so a crash cannot lose them
cross-turn dedup state is an LRU capped at 500 files to bound memory
empty diagnostic sets are never forwarded to the model
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft: a dedup failure falls back to undeduplicated files rather than dropping diagnostics

extension.name: skills-discovery-and-precedence
extension.what: Skills load from managed, user, project, --add-dir additional directories and legacy /commands/ directories, from disk as markdown with YAML frontmatter (name, description, allowed-tools, disallowed-tools, model, effort, context:fork, agent, hooks, paths, shell, user-invocable, disable-model-invocation) (src/skills/loadSkillsDir.ts:637-756, 182-265). Duplicates are removed by realpath identity with first-wins semantics (symlink-safe), and skills discovered under a file's parent directories during a session are added dynamically with deepest-path precedence, while frontmatter `paths` produce conditional skills activated for matching paths (loadSkillsDir.ts:678-722, 860-950). All of this is suppressed under isRestrictedToPluginOnly('skills') and, in --bare mode, restricted to explicit --add-dir paths.
invariants: deduplication is by realpath, not path string, so symlinked duplicates collapse
deeper (closer-to-file) skill directories win over shallower ones
a gitignored .claude/skills directory is skipped during dynamic discovery
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft: unreadable or invalid skills are logged and skipped, and a missing directory is a silent miss

extension.name: bundled-skills-registry
extension.what: Skills compiled into the CLI register programmatically into an in-memory registry that becomes Command objects with source 'bundled'; a bundled skill declaring `files` lazily extracts its reference files to a per-process nonce directory on first invocation, with a memoized promise so concurrent invocations share one extraction, and prefixes the prompt with a base-directory line (src/skills/bundledSkills.ts:54-74, 122-147, 178-221). Extraction is hardened with 0o700 and 0o600 modes, O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW and an explicit traversal check (bundledSkills.ts:178-208). initBundledSkills() registers nine skills unconditionally, but four more (dream, hunter, loop, runSkillGenerator) sit behind feature flags that are all false here and dream.ts is itself an empty stub, so those four never register (src/skills/bundled/index.ts:21-57; src/skills/bundled/dream.ts:1).
invariants: a skill-relative file path may not be absolute or contain '..'
concurrent first invocations share one extraction promise
extraction failure degrades to a skill without a base directory, not a failure
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft: extraction failure returns null and the skill still returns its prompt blocks

extension.name: hook-execution-engine
extension.what: src/utils/hooks.ts is the real hook engine, not the React hooks in src/hooks/. It merges matchers from the config snapshot, from SDK and plugin-registered hooks and from session-scoped hooks, matches them against a permission-rule-style pattern with an `if` condition matcher, then runs all matches in parallel with per-hook timeouts (src/utils/hooks.ts:1693-1812). Five hook types exist — command (shell), prompt (small-fast-model LLM returning ok/reason), http (POST with the SSRF guard and env-interpolated headers), agent (multi-turn verifier subagent) and exec (argv, no shell) — plus in-process callbacks (src/schemas/hooks.ts:33, 68, 98, 129, 166; src/utils/hooks/execHttpHook.ts:12). Exit code 2 is the protocol's block: it produces a blockingError for PreToolUse, UserPromptSubmit and Stop, while any other non-zero exit is a non-blocking error (hooks.ts:569-590, 266-273); async hooks register in AsyncHookRegistry with a default 15s timeout and asyncRewake hooks bypass the registry and wake the model on exit 2 (src/utils/hooks/AsyncHookRegistry.ts:51). Output over 50,000 chars spills to a temp file (hooks.ts:170-196).
invariants: all hooks require workspace trust in interactive mode, checked centrally before any execution
a plugin directory must exist before running a plugin hook, otherwise it throws, because exit-2-from-a-missing-script is indistinguishable from an intentional block
a hook decision of 'block' sets permissionBehavior deny but does NOT set preventContinuation; only continue:false stops the agent
extension.failurePolicy: mixed: an explicit exit 2 or decision:'block' is fail-closed (blocks the tool or prompt), while hook spawn errors, missing plugin directories, EPIPE and timeouts are fail-soft and surface as non-blocking errors

extension.name: hook-config-sources-and-policy
extension.what: Hook settings are snapshotted at init from the allowed sources with a managed-settings policy layer on top: policySettings.disableAllHooks kills every hook, policySettings.allowManagedHooksOnly restricts execution to policy hooks, strictPluginOnlyCustomization blocks user, project and local settings hooks while leaving plugin hooks intact, and disableAllHooks in non-managed settings degrades to managed-only rather than a full disable (src/utils/hooks/hooksConfigSnapshot.ts:18-88). Execution-time filtering additionally skips plugin hooks (identified by pluginRoot) and all session and frontmatter hooks when managed-only is in effect, which is what stops agent and skill frontmatter hooks from bypassing policy (src/utils/hooks.ts:1714-1751, 3669-3683).
invariants: non-managed settings can never disable managed hooks
frontmatter hooks from agents and skills are dropped entirely under managed-only
plugin hooks are not affected by strictPluginOnlyCustomization, being policy-adjacent rather than user config
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed for policy: the managed-only and disableAllHooks branches return an empty or policy-only hook set

extension.name: plugin-marketplace-management
extension.what: Marketplaces are declared in settings and materialised into known_marketplaces.json; diffMarketplaces compares the two, canonicalising relative paths against the git root so worktrees do not fight over one global entry, and reconcileMarketplaces installs the missing and re-clones the source-changed additively and idempotently, reporting per-marketplace progress to app state (src/utils/plugins/reconciler.ts:50-264). Sources are git, github, git-subdir, url, file, directory and 'settings'; the official marketplace is fetched from a GCS mirror first with a .gcs-sha sentinel and a path-containment guard, and only falls back to git (src/utils/plugins/officialMarketplaceGcs.ts:28-65; src/utils/plugins/officialMarketplaceStartupCheck.ts:216-258). Reserved official names are protected by a reserved-name set plus a homograph and impersonation regex, with validateOfficialNameSource requiring the anthropics org (src/utils/plugins/schemas.ts:19-153).
invariants: reconcile is additive — it never deletes a materialised marketplace
a reserved name may only be used by a source from the official GitHub org
seed and managed marketplaces are never auto-refreshed in bulk
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft: a failed marketplace is recorded in result.failed and surfaced in the UI while other marketplaces still reconcile

extension.name: plugin-install-and-component-integration
extension.what: Plugins install, enable, disable, uninstall and update through pluginOperations with an installable-scope whitelist (user, project, local), a V2 installed_plugins.json registry and a policy chokepoint where managed enabledPlugins[id]=false blocks install and enable at every scope (src/services/plugins/pluginOperations.ts:72; src/utils/plugins/pluginPolicy.ts:17-20; src/utils/plugins/installedPluginsManager.ts:315). Loaded plugins contribute components that become first-class harness state: MCP servers with per-server error isolation, LSP servers, hooks, commands, agents, output styles and user-configurable options substituted via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}, ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA} and ${user_config.X} (src/utils/plugins/pluginLoader.ts:3090-3140; src/utils/plugins/mcpPluginIntegration.ts:503-548; src/utils/plugins/pluginOptionsStorage.ts:356). A built-in plugin registry also exists but is INERT: initBuiltinPlugins() has an empty body and is its only caller, so BUILTIN_PLUGINS is never populated (src/plugins/bundled/index.ts:20-23; src/plugins/builtinPlugins.ts:57-102).
invariants: plugin install and enable are refused when managed policy sets enabledPlugins[id]=false
a cache-only load must never satisfy a caller that wants fresh source (separate memoize caches)
one plugin's MCP or LSP failure must not abort loading the others
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed for policy-blocked plugins; fail-soft for individual component failures, which are collected as PluginError and surfaced rather than thrown

extension.name: cron-scheduling
extension.what: The scheduling subsystem is fully implemented but entirely unreachable in this build: it would parse five-field cron expressions, persist durable jobs to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json with session-only jobs in bootstrap state, compute jittered next-fire times, auto-expire recurring jobs, detect missed one-shots for catch-up, and arbitrate a single firing session through an O_EXCL scheduler lock with PID liveness and stale-lock recovery (src/utils/cronTasks.ts:74-99; src/utils/cronTasksLock.ts:111-173; src/utils/cronScheduler.ts:40-44). Three gates all close: the CronCreate/CronDelete/CronList tools are only pushed into the tool list inside feature('AGENT_TRIGGERS'), isCronEnabled() and isDurableCronEnabled() re-check the same flag, and the REPL and print-mode scheduler hooks are behind it too (src/tools.ts:27-33; src/tools/ScheduleCronTool/prompt.ts:12-23; src/screens/REPL.tsx:183; src/cli/print.ts:320-321).
invariants: only one session may fire durable jobs; the lock is PID-liveness based with stale recovery
a durable cron cannot be created by a teammate, which would orphan the agentId
MAX_JOBS caps total scheduled jobs
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft in design (a missing or corrupt scheduled_tasks.json reads as an empty list and invalid cron strings are dropped), but moot because the mechanism is inert

extension.name: todo-durable-state
extension.what: TodoWrite stores the session checklist as durable in-memory extension state on AppState.todos keyed by agentId with the session id as fallback, returns old and new lists, clears the list when every item is completed, and requires no permission check (src/tools/TodoWriteTool/TodoWriteTool.ts:58-94). It is registered unconditionally but self-disables: isEnabled() is !isTodoV2Enabled(), and isTodoV2Enabled() is !getIsNonInteractiveSession(), so in a normal interactive REPL TodoWrite is DISABLED and the Task* tools are registered instead (TodoWriteTool.ts:52-54; src/utils/tasks.ts:133-139; src/tools.ts:187-189). The verification-nudge branch is dead twice over, requiring feature('VERIFICATION_AGENT') and a GrowthBook stub value (TodoWriteTool.ts:76-86).
invariants: todo state is per-agent (context.agentId ?? session id) so subagent lists never leak into the main thread
a fully-completed list is stored as empty, not as completed items
there is no permission gate — writes are always allowed
extension.failurePolicy: fail-open: checkPermissions always returns allow, and state loss is confined to the process

extension.name: plan-mode-and-plan-files
extension.what: Plan mode is a durable-state extension: EnterPlanMode switches the permission mode to 'plan' and is refused inside agent contexts, while ExitPlanModeV2 persists the plan to a slug-named markdown file under the plans directory, prefers an existing on-disk plan over the submitted argument when the user edited it, and on approval restores prePlanMode and sets the plan-mode-exit flags (src/tools/EnterPlanModeTool/EnterPlanModeTool.ts:66-81; src/tools/ExitPlanModeTool/ExitPlanModeV2Tool.ts:235-349). The plans directory resolves from settings.plansDirectory, validated to stay inside the project root and otherwise falling back to the config home, is created with mkdirSync and is memoized because it is called from render bodies (src/utils/plans.ts:69-134). Plan slugs are per-session with a bounded retry count, and subagent plans get a suffix so they never overwrite the main plan.
invariants: plansDirectory may not escape the project root
plans are keyed by session slug, with subagent plans suffixed so they never overwrite the main plan
ExitPlanMode restores the previously active permission mode rather than hardcoding a default
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft: a plan-file write failure is logged and the tool still returns, and a missing plan file reads as null

extension.name: tool-search-deferred-tools
extension.what: ToolSearchTool implements deferred tool loading: MCP tools and any tool with shouldDefer:true are withheld from the initial prompt, with an opt-out via _meta['anthropic/alwaysLoad'], and are loaded on demand by name (select:A,B), keyword search, or '+required term' ranking against a memoized description index invalidated when the deferred set changes (src/tools/ToolSearchTool/ToolSearchTool.ts:21-87). The tool is registered only when isToolSearchEnabledOptimistic() is true (src/tools.ts:208-210). Its location-hint text is GrowthBook-gated: the system-reminder delta variant is off in this build and the pre-gate available-deferred-tools wording is what the model sees (src/tools/ToolSearchTool/prompt.ts:28-58).
invariants: a deferred tool cannot be invoked before its schema is fetched
description memoization is keyed by tool name only and must be invalidated on deferred-set change
alwaysLoad is checked before the MCP and defer rules so an MCP tool can opt out
extension.failurePolicy: fail-soft: unknown tool names in a select query simply return no matches

extension.name: workflow-engine
extension.what: The workflow-script engine is present only as stubs: src/tools/WorkflowTool/WorkflowTool.ts exports null, createWorkflowCommand() returns null and getWorkflowCommands() returns [] so no /workflow commands materialise, and WorkflowPermissionRequest() is a null component (src/tools/WorkflowTool/WorkflowTool.ts:1; createWorkflowCommand.ts:3-9; WorkflowPermissionRequest.tsx:1-3). Registration in tools.ts and commands.ts is additionally wrapped in feature('WORKFLOW_SCRIPTS') and would require a non-existent bundled workflow module (src/tools.ts:99-102, 199; src/commands.ts:346-349). The capability is declared in the tool-name constants and permission-classifier vocabulary but has no implementation and no registration path.
extension.failurePolicy: fail-closed: nothing is registered, so no workflow can be started or permissioned
